formula.scalar_parent: P0554 radial flux remap with universal q=1.2300686115098052
formula.galaxy_and_solar_route_limit: exactly zero only for the defined axisymmetric-disk and point-source translations

copied_from_sigma_gravity: multi-domain galaxy, cluster, and Solar scorecard
strengthened_here: raw image-root completeness is separate from residual RMS
raw lensing, GR/NFW-derived lensing products, inherited scores, synthetic invariants, and analytic proxies have distinct provenance labels
all interaction bins report sample size and bootstrap uncertainty
cluster means receive leave-one-system-out influence checks
exact symmetry nulls count as compatibility checks, not positive observational evidence
per-object best phase remains diagnostic and is never promoted as a universal formula

mass_bias_reversal.interpretation: P0554 tends to underpredict dwarf outer speeds and overpredict giant outer speeds; this is a scalar amplitude/transition problem, not an angular-route effect.

gas_trend.interpretation: The raw gas trend is strong, but much of it tracks baryonic mass; use the partial correlations before adding a gas parameter.

cluster_phase_heterogeneity.interpretation: RXJ2129 supplies most of the +90-degree mean gain; the other four systems are close to neutral and have mixed signs.

differential_findings.cluster_direction_lesson: Quadrupole Q and Delta80 determine route amplitude, but the pre-existing residual-vector alignment determines whether the induced shift helps. A baryon-predicted direction is still missing.
differential_findings.topology_lesson: Small parameter or phase changes can cross caustics and lose or create roots; full root completeness must precede any RMS comparison.
differential_findings.symmetry_null_lesson: The exact galaxy and Solar route nulls protect compatibility but provide no affirmative test of the angular route physics.
differential_findings.domain_conflict_lesson: No scalar or route coordinate is both dominant and directionally consistent across galaxy rotation, raw cluster images, and Solar proxies.

next_discriminating_tests: Fit a universal scalar correction only on a development subset, then require it to remove the dwarf-to-giant residual sign reversal on untouched SPARC galaxies without using observed rotation-curve shape as an input.
Construct a baryon-only angular predictor from gas-star centroid offsets, external tidal axes, or resolved multipole orientation; freeze it before raw image scoring.
Acquire at least five new complete-baseline clusters and require every held-out root plus a leave-one-cluster-out gain that stays positive when the most responsive system is removed.
Replace Solar proxies with a joint multi-planet ephemeris likelihood before making a Solar-System compatibility claim stronger than provisional.
Report dark-matter comparisons at matched flexibility: universal formula versus both compact-halo baselines and object-specific halo fits, with parameter counts explicit.
claim_limits: The 131 SPARC galaxies and all named cluster systems are project-spent; this stage discovers conditional behavior and does not create a pristine validation set.
Galaxy morphology interactions are descriptive and are screened across many bins; bootstrap intervals quantify sampling variation but do not remove multiple-testing or model-selection bias.
Outer rotation shape uses observed velocities and therefore diagnoses failure but cannot be used as an input to a blind prediction.
The five-cluster phase scan holds lens geometry fixed; A383 is a chronological formula transfer with a full refit, while MS2137 is root-incomplete.
Raw image-root loss is a topology failure and is never converted into a favorable finite RMS.
The compact-halo comparison is a limited fitted comparator, not a proof that all dark-matter models achieve the quoted score.
Solar results are analytic proxies, not a raw multi-planet ephemeris likelihood.
No per-system phase, strength, width, or gravity constant is allowed in the promoted formula.
